references.text: Pharaoh set overseers over the Israelites to oppress them with forced labor, which is referred to here as 'their burdens' (סִבְלֹתֵיכֶם).
Describes the hard work and burdens that the Egyptians imposed on the Israelites, the same context Pharaoh refers to.
Moses saw the burdens of the Israelites (סִבְלֹתָם), the same word used here for forced labor.
God promises to free the Israelites from the burdens of the Egyptians (סִבְלֹת), a direct contrast to Pharaoh's command to return to their burdens.
Pharaoh repeats the accusation that the people are idle and therefore listen to deceitful words, the same theme of keeping them occupied with work.
Pharaoh regrets having let the people go free from their labor, showing his focus on retaining them as a workforce.
Contrasting reactions from Pharaoh: first refusing service to God, later permitting that same service.
Direct narrative contrast: Pharaoh goes from refusing service (5:4) to ordering them to go and serve the Lord (12:31).
Direct theological confrontation: Pharaoh demands labor (5:4), while God demands service through liberation (10:3).
